newsitem.title: UK: UK jobs data hide lack of worker skills - UK union.
newsitem.headline: UK jobs data hide lack of worker skills - UK union.

text.p: The fall in Britain's jobless rate in June conceals a worrying picture of skill shortages among workers, requiring more investment by employers and unions working with the government, the main umbrella body for UK unions said on Wednesday.

"Too many people do not have the skills needed for a modern economy. Investment in skills must now be an urgent priority," the Trades Union Congress (TUC) chief economist Bill Callaghan said in a statement.
He welcomed the announcement earlier today of a 5.7 percent fall in the unemployment rate in June, which is the latest indicator of strong economic growth.
The June decline reduced the jobless rate to its lowest level in more than seven years.
But Callaghan warned the strength of the pound and rising interest rates put "a question mark over hundreds of thousands of manufacturing jobs in the future."
The latest data will stoke up speculation that the UK base rate -- now 6.75 percent -- must be hiked again to cap economic growth and keep inflation in check.
British trades unions have pledged to co-operate with the new Labour government on reducing unemployment and improving working conditions for employees.
